subject: Do you train on customer data? Residency & deletion workflow
messages:
From: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@starlite.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jade Wu <jade.wu@starlite.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Question: Do you use customer data to train models? Residency & deletion process

Hi Olga,

We're evaluating Redwood for a POC and have a couple of compliance items we need to clear up before we proceed. Two quick questions: 1) Do you ever use customer request/response content to train or tune Redwood models (or any models accessible via the API)? 2) If we ask for data deletion, what is the workflow and how long until data is removed from backups/replicas?

We're particularly sensitive to EU residency for some datasets — can you confirm where data is stored for hosted customers and whether we can guarantee EU-only residency?

If easier, happy to jump on a short call. Thanks —

Liam O'Connell
Security Lead, Starlite AI
liam.oconnell@starlite.ai

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@starlite.ai>
Cc: Jade Wu <jade.wu@starlite.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T12:30:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Question: Do you use customer data to train models? Residency & deletion process

Hi Liam —

Short answer up front: Redwood does not train our models on customer-provided request/response content unless a customer explicitly opts in to a named data-contribution program. Below are the key points and how they map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments.

Hosted (redwood.ai API):
- Default: no training on customer content. By default, customer inputs are never added to model training corpora.
- Opt-in programs: we run an explicit "Research Contribution" program (rare, documented, and opt-in via contract). If a customer opts in, data is pseudonymized and aggregated before being considered for model improvements; participation and exact usage are contractual.
- Residency: hosted customers can select a region for data residency (us / eu / apac) at account creation. Data is stored in the selected region for active request processing and for short-term logs.

Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Data isolation: tenant isolation ensures customer traffic does not mix with other tenants. We still do not use customer content for training unless contractually agreed.
- Telemetry: aggregate telemetry for runtime performance may be collected unless disabled in the Dedicated config.

Private (VPC / on-prem):
- No outbound transfer: customer data stays in their network. Redwood-managed control plane can be configured to avoid pulling content into our services. "No training" is effectively enforced because data never leaves the customer's environment.

Retention & deletion (high level):
- Active request logs: retained by default for 30 days to support debugging and anomaly detection.
- Billing/usage metadata: retained for 2 years for invoicing and audit purposes (can be scoped per contract).
- Deletion request process: submit a support request with account id and the identifiers to remove (we provide an API-guided purge flow). Core infra removes data from primary stores within 48 hours of an approved request. Backups and snapshots are treated per backup retention schedule — final irrevocable removal can take up to 90 days depending on snapshot cycles.

If you need formal language for a contract or SOW, we can provide a short data handling clause and a deletion SLA. I've attached a concise retention matrix and our SOC 2 summary for your security team.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Review the attached data-retention-matrix.xlsx and the SOC 2 summary.
2) If you'd like EU-only residency, confirm the account region and we'll lock processing to eu-1.
3) If you want programmatic deletion details, see the deletion-api-guide (attached) or I can connect you with our security engineer.

Happy to schedule 20 min with you and Jade this week.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director of Sales, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Question: Do you use customer data to train models? Residency & deletion process

Thanks Olga — that covers a lot. Two follow-ups from our legal/compliance team: 1) Can you provide a written commitment clause we can use in an MSA that says Redwood will not use customer content to train models unless explicitly consented? 2) For the deletion SLA, can you clarify if the 90-day upper bound is deterministic (i.e., guaranteed) or an estimate tied to backup cycles?

Also, is there any chance model outputs could reflect proprietary customer content (i.e., leakage) even if you don't train on it? Our team will want to see mitigations.

-Liam

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connell <liam.oconnell@starlite.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T15:04:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Question: Do you use customer data to train models? Residency & deletion process

Hi Liam — thanks for the follow-ups. I'm on the security & compliance engineering team and wanted to provide the precise language and the technical deletion workflow you can use in an MSA (copy-paste friendly).

1) Sample commitment language for an MSA: "Redwood Inference will not use Customer Content (as defined in this Agreement) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any production model unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in consent to a named data-contribution program. Any such participation will be subject to a separate agreement that describes the scope, anonymization techniques, and data handling controls."

2) Deletion SLA (contractual template):
- Request acknowledgement: within 24 hours.
- Removal from primary/active systems: within 48 hours of approval.
- Final removal from periodic backups/snapshots: within 90 days.
- Certification: upon completion, Redwood will provide a deletion certificate that lists the identifiers purged.

The 90-day window is deterministic in our standard template and aligns with backup retention windows we give customers; if you require a shorter window we can discuss contract language and a custom backup cadence.

3) Leakage risk / model outputs:
- Because we do not include customer content in training corpora by default, the risk of emergent memorization of specific customer inputs in model outputs is extremely low. For Hosted customers, we also have guardrails: request/response logging is separated from any corpora pipelines.
- We additionally offer options for higher-protection profiles: private deployment, Dedicated with telemetry disabled, and response redaction hooks.

4) Programmatic deletion endpoint (technical):
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/accounts/{account_id}/data/purge
- Authentication: API key with admin scope or support ticket + approval token.
- Operation: purge accepts object ids, date ranges, and scopes (requests, embeddings, logs). A job id is returned; you can poll GET /jobs/{job_id}/status. Primary store purge completes within 48 hours; job will report when the primary purge is done and when the snapshot purge is scheduled.

I've attached the deletion-api-guide.md with example curl snippets and the retention matrix for easy mapping to different data classes. If you'd like, I can prepare the MSA clause and deletion SLA as part of a redlined exhibit and send to your counsel.

Would you like me to open a support case to demonstrate a test purge on a sandbox account?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
